Hey Linos,

Sorry for the delay in answering your question; I took a few days off from trading and just now looked at my journal. You ask some great questions, and I will do my best to answer them for you. One disclaimer though...I am FAR from where I need to be as a trader and I don't want to lead you (or anyone else) down the wrong path. I'll simply tell you what my thought process was on this trade

I chose the LS level because of its proximity to the engulf of the FL it was located inside. In my opinion, the best LS are ones closely related to the high/low it precedes. I saw the engulf of the 'high' and chose the LS based on it being the last potential shoulder that formed prior to the engulf. That was my only criteria for choosing the LS. I drew the "kink" accordingly. Here are two charts to illustrate:

Not every kink is reactive... some work really well and others don't. I still haven't been able to determine a way to know with 90%+ certainty which kinks will bounce price and which ones will get blown through. With that said, a couple of weeks ago I analyzed 50 kinks...roughly half of them were successful and half were not. The common denominator fond in nearly all of the "winning" kinks (ones that bounces price) was LTF PA confirmation of a fractal IQM. I always look for this extra piece of confirming PA and it has kept me on the right side of many kink trades ever since. Here is a LTF IQM/Kink I found on the USD-JPY example:

Hopefully this helps you understand my thought process..I still have a very long way to go as a trader, and I still have questions about what technically constitutes an "ignored" QM. I am still working on these concepts, but so far, I am really having luck when it comes to finding fractal IQM's within higher scale IQM's.

author: hoeschec
text:
Staurum's recent post on my journal has me thinking...I need to add another "filter" to my analysis when it comes to trading hidden kinks.

My main "filter" is to look for a fractal IQM's as confirmation for a low risk entry. After looking at Staurum's response to my post (his post is above here, on post # 1858) however, I need to ask if my kink zone is located within a higher time frame compression zone. Let's take this one step further....I need to ask: is the kink located within a PAZ? If so, is it located in the middle of the PAZ or at the edge of the PAZ?

I use filters as a way to 'weed out' weak setups with too much risk. In my experience, the best filters are simple yes/no if/then questions. These filters need to be highly objective or else it gets too confusing/complex.

author: staurum
text:
"is the kink located within a PAZ? If so, is it located in the middle of the PAZ or at the edge of the PAZ?"

PAZ in a scale/range/size is limited by a Flag Limit or Kink or "King" Once we get this, we need to zoom in (or peek) where the "King" is hiding the "Queen Majesty" / QM / Quasimodo / the "King's Maximum Pain Level MPL". lol... sorry for the jokes, i just played cards with kids going crazy not knowing the difference between King cards and Queen cards.

Anyway, back to chart. I was looking for poles essentially (remember CP = Pole), because i want to know there is the FL that ends the pole so that i know when that FL is broken, it will target the polebase. Otherwise, the FL that ends the pole will be met with another FL from the opposite direction to ping-pong the price within the FLAG / PAZ. rest is finding out if price is trying to bounce at the FLAG limits by watching an Engulf PA. Or when it breaks the FL, which polebase it's trying to target. Therefore, to sum up again. FL is always at PAZ edge.

Regarding the little blue kink, yes it's one, but i would prefer watching the kink that engulfs the whole CPPAZ and fails to return to it (it be CPPAZ).
